## Proposition 13.5
**Statement:** If a straight line be cut in extreme and mean ratio, and there be added to it a straight line equal to the greater segment, the whole straight line has been cut in extreme and mean ratio, and the original straight line is the greater segment.

Let the straight line AB be cut in extreme and mean ratio at the point C, AC being the greater segment, and let the straight line AD, equal to AC, be added to AB at the end A, so that D, A, B lie in one straight line with A between D and B. I say that DB has been cut in extreme and mean ratio at A, and that the original straight line AB is the greater segment.

**Step 1.** Since AB has been cut in extreme and mean ratio at C, and AC is the greater segment, by the definition of extreme and mean ratio, as the whole AB is to the greater segment AC, so is AC to the lesser segment CB [D6.3].

**Step 2.** Therefore, inversely, as AC is to AB, so is CB to AC [5.7, Porism].

**Step 3.** Since AD is equal to AC, the equal magnitudes AD and AC have the same ratio to the same magnitude AB; therefore, as AD is to AB, so is AC to AB [5.7]. But as AC is to AB, so is CB to AC (Step 2); therefore, as AD is to AB, so is CB to AC [5.11].

**Step 4.** The magnitudes AD, AB, CB, AC are thus proportional separando; therefore they are also proportional componendo: as AD together with AB is to AB, so is CB together with AC to AC [5.18]. Now AD together with AB is the whole DB, since A lies between D and B; and CB together with AC is the whole AB, since C lies between A and B. Therefore, as DB is to AB, so is AB to AC.

**Step 5.** Again, since AC is equal to AD, the same magnitude AB has the same ratio to the equal magnitudes AC and AD; therefore, as AB is to AC, so is AB to AD [5.7]. But as DB is to AB, so is AB to AC (Step 4); therefore, as DB is to AB, so is AB to AD [5.11].

**Step 6.** Now DB is greater than AB, for the whole is greater than the part [CN5]. And since the first DB has to the second AB the same ratio as the third AB has to the fourth AD, and the first DB is greater than the third AB, the second AB is also greater than the fourth AD [5.14].

**Step 7.** Therefore the straight line DB has been cut at A so that, as the whole DB is to the greater segment AB, so is the greater segment AB to the lesser segment AD. Hence DB has been cut in extreme and mean ratio at A [D6.3], and the original straight line AB is the greater segment. Q.E.D.

*Path note:* An alternative route exists through areas — converting the hypothesis to rect(AB, BC) = sq(AC) by 6.17, showing rect(DB, DA) = sq(AB) by 2.3 and 2.2, and converting back by 6.17. The proportional route above is chosen because D6.3 is itself stated as a proportion and the conclusion follows from two Book 5 manipulations (inversion and componendo) without passing through areas.

I say that the straight line DB has been cut in extreme and mean ratio at A, and the original straight line AB is the greater segment. For let the square AE be described on AB, and let the figure be drawn. Since AB has been cut in extreme and mean ratio at C, therefore the rectangle AB, BC is equal to the square on AC. [VI. Def. 3, VI. 17] And CE is the rectangle AB, BC, and CH the square on AC; therefore CE is equal to HC. But HE is equal to CE, and DH is equal to HC; therefore DH is also equal to HE. Therefore the whole DK is equal to the whole AE. And DK is the rectangle BD, DA, for AD is equal to DL; and AE is the square on AB; therefore the rectangle BD, DA is equal to the square on AB. Therefore, as DB is to BA, so is BA to AD. [VI. 17] And DB is greater than BA; therefore BA is also greater than AD. [V. 14] Therefore DB has been cut in extreme and mean ratio at A, and AB is the greater segment.
